name: Gardner-Robertson Hearing Classification

version.label: Gardner-Robertson modified hearing classification (1988)
version.detail: Class from pure-tone average (PTA) and speech discrimination score (SDS). I 0–30 dB / 70–100%; II 31–50 dB / 50–69%; III 51–90 dB / 5–49%; IV 91 dB to maximum / 1–4%; V not testable / 0%. The AAO-HNS (1995) A–D hearing classes are a different system and are not combined.

purpose: Classifies hearing in the affected ear, mainly in vestibular schwannoma, using audiometry.
intendedPopulation: Patients with vestibular schwannoma or other cerebellopontine angle lesions, with pure-tone and speech audiometry.

calculatorNotice.title: When PTA and SDS disagree
calculatorNotice.message: Published descriptions disagree on which class to use when PTA and SDS fall in different classes (some use the better, others the poorer). The app does not choose: it reports both classes.

inputDefinitions.label: Pure-tone average (PTA)
inputDefinitions.help: Use the PTA as defined by your audiology service (commonly 0.5, 1, 2 and 3 kHz, or 0.5, 1 and 2 kHz) and state which.

calculationMethod.share: Gardner-Robertson {total == 0 ? 'discordant (PTA class ' + roman(pta) + ', SDS class ' + roman(sds) + ')' : 'class ' + roman(total)}

resultStates.label: Discordant: PTA class {roman(pta)}, SDS class {roman(sds)}
resultStates.summary: PTA and SDS fall in different classes.
resultStates.detail: Sources apply different rules in this situation, so no single class is assigned. Report both values, and the rule used if your service has one.

resultStates.label: Class I: good to excellent
resultStates.summary: PTA 0–30 dB and SDS 70–100% at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Describes audiometric hearing in the tested ear; it does not predict whether hearing will be preserved.

resultStates.label: Class II: serviceable
resultStates.detail: Classes I–II are usually described as serviceable hearing.

resultStates.label: Class IV: poor
resultStates.summary: PTA 91 dB to maximum and SDS 1–4%.
resultStates.detail: Assess with the full audiological picture according to the clinical situation; describes hearing in the tested ear only.

resultStates.label: Class V: none
resultStates.detail: Assess with the full audiological picture according to the clinical situation; describes hearing in the tested ear only.

clinicalContext.text: Classifies hearing in the affected ear from standard audiometry.
Widely used to report hearing preservation after surgery or radiosurgery for vestibular schwannoma.

clinicalInsights.text: Discordant PTA and SDS: report both classes rather than one.
State the frequencies used for the PTA; definitions differ between studies.

limitations.text: No agreed rule when PTA and SDS fall in different classes.

limitations: PTA frequency sets differ between studies.
Does not capture tinnitus, vestibular function or subjective hearing handicap.

confounders.effect: Change SDS values between languages and centres.
Raises PTA independent of the tumour.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: The likelihood of preserving hearing with any treatment.

guideSections.what: A five-class hearing classification (I–V) from pure-tone average and speech discrimination.
guideSections.whenToUse: Reporting hearing before and after treatment of vestibular schwannoma and other cerebellopontine angle lesions.
guideSections.howToPerform: Obtain pure-tone and speech audiometry for the affected ear. Select the PTA band and the SDS band. If both are in the same class, that is the class; if not, report both.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A reporting classification; treatment decisions consider tumour size, growth, symptoms and patient preference.

sources.citation: Gardner G, Robertson JH. Hearing preservation in unilateral acoustic neuroma surgery. Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol. 1988;97(1):55-66.

Hörklassen bei Patienten mit Vestibularisschwannom bei Verwendung deutschsprachiger Testverfahren (Hearing classes in vestibular schwannoma with German-language tests). HNO. 2021. Notes the conflicting rules for discordant PTA and SDS.
